newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian farmer protests grow bigger, talks held.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian farmer protests grow bigger, talks held.

text.p: Thousands of farmers blocked roads in Hungary for a second day on Tuesday as government and farmer leaders held closed-door talks to try to end a protest over tax changes.
Radio and media reports said farmers driving tractors, ploughs, harvesters and occasionally family cars were out in bigger numbers than on Monday, the first day of the three-day protest.
The protests continued as a five-person government delegation led by Finance Ministry State Secretary Tibor Draskovics held closed-door talks with leaders of the protests by smallhold farmers.
The Hungarian MTI news agency quoted Zoltan Buda, a farmer representative attending the talks in Kiskoros, central Hungary, as saying that no agreement was likely on Tuesday.

"One cannot count on an agreement today because neither the small farmers nor the ministry can come to a mutual or a joint result about the amendments of the bill on tax and social insurance," the agency reported Buda as saying.
The farmers are protesting at the end of an exemption from social security contributions as of January 1 and new requirements to provide documentation for tax purposes.

National police had no immediate estimates of the numbers of farmers participating in the protests, but radio and media reports said it was more than the 7,000 who took part in the demonstrations on Monday in eight of Hungary's 19 counties.
There were no reports of violence and police directed traffic to alternate routes so that motorists could avoid delays.
The protest leaders have said they will end the road blockades on Wednesday but that protests could resume if the government does not meet their demands.

Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy, who did not attend the Kiskoros talks, said earlier the government was prepared to modify the new tax law but would not reinstate the social security exemptions for farmers or eliminate documentation requirements because this would create inequities in the system.
Farmers said they were increasingly frustrated by the government's position.

"If there is no agreement we are ready to continue our demonstration at any time because we have no choice and we have nothing to lose," Istvan Gargyan, a farmer from eastern Csongrad county, told MTI.
